text:
Low carbohydrate intake does not result in greater reliance on muscle glycogen during exercise because depleted glycogen stores force the body to rely more heavily on fat for fuel. Furthermore, it fails to increase fat oxidation enough to improve high-intensity performance, as such efforts typically require rapid energy from carbohydrates rather than fats. Consequently, neither of these outcomes is a direct result of low carbohydrate consumption in this context.
CONFIDENCE: 100
